summary: Kogen Mizuno was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who received his Doctorate of Letters from the University of Tokyo in 1928. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo and as a professor and president at Komazawa University.
Koichi Furusaka, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He was attested as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University in 1991.
Koichi Hiraoka works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he is attested as a guest professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

Koichi Hokazono, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He held positions at Kyushu University and The International University of Kagoshima.

Koichi Hoshina was a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1894 to 1897. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1902–1933) and the Tokyo University of Education.

Koichi Shinohara is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He served as a professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004) and as a senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2018).

Koichi Takahashi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo in 2004 under Akira Saitō and Yasunori Ejima, and later held research and professorial posts at the University of Tokyo.

Koichi Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his MA at the University of Tokyo, studying under Akira Hirakawa and Gyoin Hashimoto. He was an assistant professor at Rikkyo University from circa 1974 to 2005.
Koin Takada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1944). A disciple of Gyoin Hashimoto, he succeeded him in 1967.

Koji Kamioka was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara. He was a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University in 1969 and a staff member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Shindo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who was a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies. He served as a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Bukkyo University, earning a doctorate in literature in 1991. He served as an assistant professor and professor at Bukkyo University between circa 1969 and 2005.

Kojun Fukui was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Waseda University, studying under Sokichi Tsuda. He served as a professor at Waseda University (1941–1969) and as president of Taisho University.
Kojun Saito, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 1965.
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University, attested between 1995 and 2002.

Koken Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from 1950 to 1960. He had a long career at Rissho University, serving as an assistant professor, department chair, director, professor, and professor emeritus.
Koki Kawagishi was a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 1976 as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University.
Konan Naito was a Sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Akita Normal School from 1881 to 1885. He held an academic post at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1926.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held an affiliation with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2014.

Konrad Klaus specializes in Indology and Tibetology, having studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. Between 1999 and 2001, he held deputy professorships at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn.
